input.description: Bedding. Linen. Actually-breathable stuff made in Portugal. Our customers are mostly people who got tired of the Brooklinen/Parachute aesthetic and want something a little more grown-up.

brief.statusReason: The advertiser clearly states they sell breathable bedding and linen manufactured in Portugal for mature consumers.
brief.productSummary: Premium bedding and linen sheets made in Portugal for adults seeking high-quality home goods, priced at a premium level.
assumptions: Assumed a typical single order value of $200 based on standard pricing for premium Portuguese linen sheet sets.
Assumed target age skew starts around 30, based on the description of customers wanting a 'more grown-up' aesthetic than starter premium brands.
Assumed one-time purchase model, as bedding is typically bought on an as-needed basis.

plan.reviewNote: The media plan is anchored by high-intent home design publishers, while selectively utilizing mature, high-income apparel audiences to reach our core target demographic of affluent women. This dual approach balances immediate category relevance with broader brand building among consumers who appreciate heritage quality.

creatives.whyThisPersona: This persona values enduring heritage and high-end materials over passing trends, making them the perfect match for premium Portuguese craftsmanship.

config.name: Premium bedding and linen sheets made in Portugal for adults (draft)

bidding.rationale: Start on CPM bids for 14 days to buy reach and collect conversion data (there is no history yet), then switch to a target CPA once each publisher has ~30 conversions.

creativeRotation.strategy: Even rotation for 14 days, then shift weight to the best CTR per publisher.

assumptions: No budget given: assumed $10,000 for a 30-day test.
CPMs are estimated from each audience's income tier (+15% for audiences under 5M monthly impressions); real prices come from the auction.
One-time purchase: target CPA = 30% of order value as a margin-safe default.
No publisher gets more than 25% of its monthly impressions, so no single audience is saturated.
Assumed a typical single order value of $200 based on standard pricing for premium Portuguese linen sheet sets.
Assumed target age skew starts around 30, based on the description of customers wanting a 'more grown-up' aesthetic than starter premium brands.
Assumed one-time purchase model, as bedding is typically bought on an as-needed basis.

output.understanding: The advertiser sells premium, breathable linen bedding crafted in Portugal, targeting design-conscious, affluent adults seeking a more mature and sophisticated aesthetic than mainstream direct-to-consumer bedding brands.

publishers.rationale: As a dedicated bedding and home textiles publisher with a design-conscious, high-income audience and a very high AOV of $164, Northbed represents the perfect contextual and demographic fit for high-end Portuguese linen.

Hearthstone Goods captures a high-income, design-centric demographic focused on non-toxic, sustainable home products and luxury lifestyle pieces, aligning with premium bedding upgrades and household life events.

excluded.reason: Swiftcart is focused on low-AOV convenience and instant delivery, which does not match the luxury positioning or considered purchase behavior of premium bedding buyers.
Movewell is centered on activewear and fitness subscriptions, which has minimal contextual overlap with high-end linen sheets.
Studiogrid is an appointment-based wellness service publisher with low contextual alignment for physical premium home goods.
Marlowe & Co. focuses exclusively on mid-life women's apparel, making it less contextually relevant than dedicated home design platforms.
Linden Park targets classic clothing and conservative workwear, which represents a demographic mismatch compared to design-forward home interior sites.
Everbody focuses on inclusive sizing workwear and intimates, lacking the home-decor context needed for high-AOV bedding.
Pawline targets pet owners interested in health food and subscriptions, which is irrelevant to luxury home textiles.
Pantrygood targets organic grocery and subscription shoppers, which has weaker synergy than direct home and kitchen design publishers.
Ruffco is a pet-focused platform with a broad nationwide demographic that lacks the luxury-specific lifestyle affinity required for premium bedding.
Heartfoot focuses on socks and basic undergarments, which lacks the high-end, slow-fashion positioning of Portuguese linen.
Daily Form is a scientific vitamins and supplements platform, which does not align with the tactile, aesthetic-driven purchasing of premium home textiles.
Velvetline targets Gen Z and younger millennial cosmetics shoppers with a lower AOV, which is too youthful and budget-sensitive for this high-end product.
Kitchenly targets high-frequency family meal kits, which is too utility-focused and convenience-driven for luxury linen bedroom items.
Stride & Stem is a sustainable footwear brand; while professional, it is less direct than dedicated bedding and home product networks.
Cloudfoot is focused on technical and comfortable footwear for urban professionals, presenting low category affinity with premium bed linens.
Tailcrate caters to dog toys and treats, which does not match the luxury home aesthetic.
Strandlab is a beauty and personalized haircare platform, which is too far removed from home goods.
Pop & Sip is focused on functional beverages, which is an impulse purchase category with no relation to high-end home textiles.
